direction_note: Cycle 7: scrapped fx_liquidity_withdrawal_reversal (spread-state fade zero gross on 160 USDJPY episodes; plain one-hour shock fade -0.068 R t -4.5 on 2075 trades: intraday moves continue by about 2 percent of their size, below cost; liquidity-provision family closed). Registered, revised with the Critic, built, code-reviewed and tested jpy_fiscal_year_end_repatriation: verdict scrap at the pipeline (check -0.034 R pooled, walk-forward -0.025 R, negative at 1.5x costs) and at the pre-registered per-leg rule 1 read from all 24 stage A cells. ye_short: every March-only cell lost in design (-0.022 to -0.093 R, t -0.27 to -1.23), the best hypothesis cell (mar_sep n5 sl0.25) made +0.026 R t 0.25 with clustered t 0.21 and -0.034 R without its best month-window; the ordinary-month controls were better in design (+0.025 to +0.060 R) and in check (+0.035 to +0.155 R), so the fiscal excess is negative and the Tokyo-session short in the last weekdays of a month is a generic, cost-level month-end pattern, not a fiscal flow. ny_long: every April/October cell lost in design (-0.083 to -0.111 R) while check was positive (+0.04 to +0.13 R) against negative controls, the 2021-2023 USDJPY rally drift the Critic predicted, not a flow; gotobi removal changed nothing (chosen cell +0.022 R without gotobi dates); median stop 21.4 pips, fill spread 0.63 pips as pre-registered. Lesson for the next Director to record: Japanese fiscal-calendar repatriation and new-year outflows do not show up as a tradeable spot flow in Tokyo hours net of costs; do not retry with other day counts, the London session, the fix minute, the half-year only, or JPY crosses as primary. Programme status: with the month-of-year dimension now measured, every dimension reachable from price, quote and clock data has been conditioned on at least once (clock, weekday, k-th weekday, holiday, gotobi, fiscal month, level, move size, volume, spread, cross-asset state, carry, positioning) and 7 cycles plus the gj-strat scans are all negative; further cycles on this data store will be re-slices. Recommendation to the user: pause the /research-cycle loop until external data is added (scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail positioning, options risk reversals and implied vol, FX swap basis) or redirect the loop to basket sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket for the Alpha Swing pass probability, which is a simulation task.

judgments.lesson: The quoted-spread state does not identify tradeable liquidity concessions on USDJPY at the intraday horizon, and the liquidity-provision family (conditioning on clock, level, size, tick volume and now spread) is closed. The hypothesis cell (one-hour move >= 0.25 x ATR20 with the M15 spread proxy >= 2 x its same-slot median, scheduled releases and the rollover excluded, two-hour time exit) had 160 design episodes on 123 trading days and made -0.020 R net (t -0.31; clustered t +0.22) with a gross of exactly 0.000 R on bid/ask fills, so the concession is competed away before a market order fills; the one-bar delay arm made -0.058 R (t -0.94); check was -0.065 and -0.081 R; the 0.40 x ATR cells -0.078 and -0.107 R. The no-spread-condition control measured the plain one-hour intraday shock fade on USDJPY for the first time at scale: -0.068 R (t -4.5, 2075 trades, every design year negative, gross -0.039 R before commission) and -0.073 R in check (t -4.2, 1629 trades); news-inclusive -0.070 R on 3576 trades. So one-hour moves of a quarter ATR keep going for the next two hours, by about 2 percent of the move on mid prices, which is below the 0.05 R round-trip cost: the spread condition recovered +0.048 R of that loss (below the +0.08 R pre-registered threshold) but nothing more, the news-inclusive arm was no different (-0.004 vs -0.020 R, inside the 0.05 R bound: no overreaction to scheduled news either), the fill spread was 0.89 pips so cost was not the cause, and the only positive pocket (28 episodes inside the 23:50 UTC Japan-data and 06:30 BoJ windows, +0.47 R) is a post-hoc cluster of information events and is not to be chased. Do not register the follow-the-move mirror (its gross edge of about 0.02-0.04 R is less than the cost and its sign was read off this run), do not retry with M5 or H1 bars, tighter or looser spread ratios, other move sizes, limit entries (the executor pays the spread on limits too), or EURUSD and gold as the primary, and do not use the spread ratio as a filter on any other idea.
judgments.notes: Killed at GA_stage_a_floor on USDJPY with 9.7 s of compute. The design did its job: the control arm was in the stage A grid, the kill arithmetic was fixed before the run after the Critic's revision, and the result is unambiguous in both directions (the hypothesis cell is flat at zero gross; the control is strongly negative on two thousand trades). This closes the last unused dimension of the price-and-quote store: clock, calendar day types, levels, move size, volume and spread have all been conditioned on and none makes an intraday USDJPY fade pay.

hypotheses.title: Japanese fiscal-calendar flows in Tokyo hours: short USDJPY in the last business days of March (and September) when exporters and institutions repatriate and square books for the fiscal year-end, long USDJPY in the first business days of April (and October) when new-year outward allocations start; each leg with a same-window ordinary-month control arm
hypotheses.rationale: Mechanism: about 70 percent of listed Japanese companies close their fiscal year on 31 March (half-year on 30 September). Exporters and their overseas subsidiaries repatriate foreign-currency earnings to book them and fund year-end dividends and tax; corporate treasuries and banks square foreign-currency exposures for the balance-sheet date; life insurers, pension funds and the GPIF rebalance to fiscal-year targets. These participants must trade by a date, they execute in Tokyo hours (the Tokyo cash session and the 09:55 JST fix), and the flow is one-way (sell USD, buy JPY) and concentrated in the last two weeks of March. After 1 April the sign reverses: life insurers and pension funds deploy new-fiscal-year foreign-asset allocations, and Toshin launches cluster in April (the dealer convention of April yen selling). The other side is dealers and speculators who know the convention; the gotobi edge (post-fix short +0.14 R design, +0.11 R check, gj-strat) shows that known, dated, obligated Tokyo-hour flows still move price in this data set, and the gotobi month-end-only variant (94 trades, design +0.176 R, check +0.393 R, gotobi_tweaks) shows month-end Tokyo flows are larger than ordinary gotobi flows. This hypothesis asks whether fiscal month-ends carry a flow beyond the ordinary month-end and month-start, which the control arm measures directly. Why this is new: the flow atlas conditioned on clock x weekday, gotobi, k-th-last weekday and holiday-adjacent day types but never on the month of the year, so the fiscal calendar is the one calendar dimension the 600,912-test scan did not cover; the month-end hedge (Melvin-Prins) is an equity-hedge flow at the London 4pm fix on every month-end and is dead after 2018; the Tokyo-fix tests traded a fix minute, not the session; the gold autumn seasonal tested a diffuse festival demand with no settlement date and died, and its lesson is scoped to gold. This is a dealer convention, not a published anomaly, so it is an out-of-sample test of the convention. Design: M15 bars on USDJPY (0.6 pip median spread; about 0.7-0.9 pips at the Tokyo open), market entry at 00:00 UTC (09:00 JST, Tokyo cash open), time exit at 06:00 UTC (15:00 JST, cash close), stop 0.25 or 0.5 x ATR20, no target; one trade per selected weekday. Two legs: ye_short (last n_days weekdays of the fiscal-end months, SHORT USDJPY) and ny_long (first n_days weekdays of the new-year months, LONG USDJPY). Three month sets: mar (March / April only), mar_sep (March+September / April+October) and ctrl (the same windows in the ordinary months 1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11; June and December are excluded as quarter and calendar year-ends). Counts (design 2010-2017, from the calendar, no outcomes): ye_short mar n10 = 80 trades, mar_sep n10 = 160, ctrl n10 = 480; n5 halves these; check 2018-2023 has 60 / 120 / 360. Costs: round trip about 1.7 pips (0.6-0.9 spread, 0.7 commission, 0.4 slippage) = about 0.10 R at the 0.25 x ATR stop (about 17 pips in the design years), 0.05 R at 0.5 x ATR. Expected: if the fiscal flow moves USDJPY an extra 3-4 pips per Tokyo session beyond ordinary days, the March cell nets about +0.10 R at sl 0.25 with sd about 0.7 R, design t about 1.2-1.5 on 80 trades (lower on the mar_sep cell if September is weaker); the control should sit near zero or slightly positive (the gotobi month-end effect leaks into it on 2 of every 10 days). With these counts the stage A floor passes with only about 55-60 percent probability if the effect is real, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence. Human execution: two orders a day on at most 20 days a year, placed at 09:00 JST with a time exit at 15:00 JST; trivially executable on a prop account and uncorrelated in time with the vol-box, gotobi and M-3 legs except on the 2-3 gotobi dates inside each window.
hypotheses.rules:
All times UTC. Bars: M15, sparse; locate every time by timestamp with F.first_bar_at_or_after and never assume one bar per slot.

DATE SELECTION (calendar dates, UTC): dates = unique F.utc_dates(m) with F.weekday(d) < 5 and d >= start. month(d) = calendar month number of d (1..12).
- Month sets by p['months']: if 'mar': H_short = {3}, H_long = {4}; if 'mar_sep': H_short = {3, 9}, H_long = {4, 10}; if 'ctrl': H_short = H_long = {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11}.
- Leg p['leg'] = 'ye_short': select d with month(d) in H_short and F.kth_last_weekday(dates)[d] in {0, 1, ..., n_days - 1} (the last n_days weekdays of the month; 0 = last weekday). Side = SHORT.
- Leg p['leg'] = 'ny_long': select d with month(d) in H_long and rank(d) in {0, 1, ..., n_days - 1}, where rank(d) = np.busday_count(first calendar day of d's month, d) = the number of weekdays in the month strictly before d (0 for the first weekday of the month; default Mon-Fri weekmask, no holidays). Side = LONG.
- Japanese and other holidays are not excluded (no calendar in the engine); the flow is simply absent on those days.

ENTRY: ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, 0, 0) (entry_utc '00:00'). Skip the date if ei < 1, or ei >= m.n, or m.ts[ei] is more than max_delay_min (10) minutes after d 00:00 UTC. sig = ei - 1, so the fill is at the open of bar ei (ask for longs, bid for shorts, plus slippage). entry_short[sig] = True (ye_short) or entry_long[sig] = True (ny_long); entry_type[sig] = 0; valid_bars[sig] = 1.

STOP: ATR20 = F.atr_prev(F.daily_bars(m), atr_n = 20) mapped to bars with daily.to_bars (known at the start of the trading day). Skip the date if ATR20[ei] is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = sl_atr x ATR20[ei] (price units, > 0). tp_dist = NaN (no target). max_bars = 0.

EXIT: xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, d, 6, 0) (exit_utc '06:00'). Skip the date if xi >= m.n or xi <= ei. exit_short[xi - 1] = True (ye_short) or exit_long[xi - 1] = True (ny_long), so the position closes at the open of the first bar at or after 06:00 UTC. No other exits, no filters, one trade per selected date; the executor blocks overlapping entries.

PARAMETERS (every one read from p): leg (grid 'ye_short', 'ny_long'), months (grid 'mar', 'mar_sep', 'ctrl'), n_days (grid 5, 10), sl_atr (grid 0.25, 0.5); fixed entry_utc '00:00', exit_utc '06:00', max_delay_min 10, atr_n 20, start '2010-01-01'. Grid = 24 cells. The 'ctrl' cells are control arms: they run at stage A only; stages B, C, the walk-forward and any holdout use months in {'mar', 'mar_sep'} (16 cells), set in the spec after the review step.

REPORTING (stage A table and stage C, computed from the trades): per cell the number of trades, avg R, trade-level t, month-window-clustered t (R averaged per calendar month of the entry date, then a t over those month means), mean fill spread in pips, by-year avg R; for the chosen cell the avg R and count after removing gotobi dates (F.is_gotobi) and the avg R without the best two month-windows.

pre_registered.kill_if: (1) Hypothesis-cell floor on USDJPY, applied by the Director even if the pipeline reports a candidate (the automatic stage A gate ranks all 24 cells by design t and a 480-trade control cell can outrank an 80-trade hypothesis cell): the best cell with months in {mar, mar_sep} must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and month-window-clustered t >= 1 with at least 80 trades; otherwise scrap. The chosen cell is that best hypothesis cell; its leg, n_days and sl_atr fix the comparisons below. (2) Control: avg R(chosen cell) minus avg R(the ctrl cell with the same leg, n_days and sl_atr) must be >= +0.06 R in design; if the ordinary months earn as much in the same window, the effect is the generic month-end or month-start Tokyo pattern that the atlas's last-weekday and k-th-weekday day types and the gotobi month-end variant already measured, and the hypothesis dies with that lesson. (3) Gotobi separation: design avg R at the chosen cell must stay > 0 after removing gotobi dates (F.is_gotobi: 5th, 10th, 15th, 20th, 25th and month-end, weekend dates moved back to Friday); if it does not, the result is the gotobi short again (measured, including its month-end-only variant) and the hypothesis is dead. (4) Regime and clustering: at least 4 of the 8 design years positive at the chosen cell, and design avg R must stay > 0 after removing the best two month-windows; a result carried by one or two Marches is scrapped as an episode, not a flow. (5) Costs: the hard gate (positive at 1.5x costs) stands; the mean fill spread is reported; if the chosen cell is positive gross but negative net, the lesson is that the fiscal flow exists but moves USDJPY by less than about 2 pips per Tokyo session and cannot be traded from the open. (6) Replication: the repatriation is against every foreign currency, so at the chosen cell the design avg R pooled over EURJPY, AUDJPY and GBPJPY must be > 0, and the pooled-check hard gate (avg R > 0 with >= 30 trades) and the walk-forward gate stand; a USDJPY-only result with the crosses negative is scrapped as noise. (7) Legs are separate claims with their own pre-registered sign: if only one leg passes rules 1-6 the other is scrapped with its lesson and the survivor goes forward alone; neither leg's sign is ever flipped. Honest expectation: about +0.10 R net at sl 0.25 on 80 March trades, design t 1.2-1.5, mar_sep weaker if September is a smaller flow; the stage A floor passes with only about 55-60 percent probability if the effect is real at that size, so a kill is weak evidence and a pass is strong evidence; the most likely failure is that the flow is spread over London hours and hedged forward rather than executed spot in Tokyo, which would show as a control-sized or zero result.

hypotheses.why_different: Every calendar test in the index conditioned on weekday, k-th-last weekday, gotobi or holiday-adjacent day types (the atlas: clock x those day types x currency strength; M-3; month-end hedge at the London fix; gotobi and its 40 tweaks including the month-end-only and run-up variants), or on a fix minute (Tokyo fix long, holiday-shifted fix). None conditioned on the month of the year, so the fiscal calendar is the one calendar dimension the 600,912-test scan left unmeasured, and this hypothesis is not a re-slice of a scanned slot: the slot (one month, one session, one direction) is fixed by the mechanism before any data is seen, so the family-wise error is the 24-cell grid, not the atlas's 600k tests, which is the same logic the programme applies to every pre-registered hypothesis. The gold autumn test was a diffuse festival demand with no settlement deadline and its lesson is scoped to gold; here the participant is obligated by a balance-sheet date, as the gotobi importers are by their settlement date, and the control arm measures the generic month-end component that the gotobi month-end variant already showed to exist, so the test isolates the fiscal excess. The ny_long leg is not a snooped flip of ye_short: it is a different month, a different participant (new-year outward investors) and its sign comes from the mechanism, registered here before any run.

director.direction_note: Cycle 7 scraps the liquidity-withdrawal test with a lesson that closes the liquidity-provision family: the spread-conditioned fade was exactly zero gross on 160 USDJPY episodes, and the control measured the plain one-hour intraday shock fade on USDJPY at -0.068 R (t -4.5) on 2,075 design trades and -0.073 R in check, so intraday moves continue by about 2 percent of their size on mid prices, less than the round-trip cost, and the follow mirror must not be registered. One hypothesis is registered, chosen because it is the last calendar dimension the atlas did not scan (month of the year) attached to a dated, obligated Tokyo-hour participant, the only kind of flow that has survived in this data: Japanese fiscal year-end repatriation (short USDJPY in Tokyo hours in the last business days of March and September) and new-fiscal-year outflows (long in the first business days of April and October), each with a same-window ordinary-month control, gotobi separation and a three-cross replication; 24 cells, 80-160 hypothesis trades in design, expected +0.10 R and t 1.2-1.5, stage A floor about 55-60 percent likely to pass if real. After the review step the Director must set specs/auto/jpy_fiscal_year_end_repatriation.json so that stage_a carries the full 24-cell grid (controls included) and the spec grid for stages B, C and the walk-forward holds months in {mar, mar_sep} only, as was done for the liquidity test; the Builder needs no new engine helper (first-n-weekdays rank is np.busday_count from the month start). Programme status for the user: with this registration every dimension reachable from price, quote and clock data has been conditioned on at least once (clock, weekday, k-th weekday, holiday, gotobi, fiscal month, level, move size, volume, spread, cross-asset state, carry, positioning); if this test is negative, further cycles on this data store will be re-slices and should stop. The next useful inputs are external: a scheduled-event calendar with surprise sizes, retail long/short positioning, options risk reversals and implied vol, and the FX swap basis; without them the remaining lever for the Alpha Swing pass probability is the sizing and risk design of the existing USDJPY basket, which is a simulation task for the engine rather than a hypothesis for this loop.

reasons: This is not a duplicate, and it deserves compute. I checked run_flow_atlas.py. Its day types are weekdays, gotobi, month-start and month-end ordinals, and US, Japan and England holidays. There is no calendar-month condition, so the month-of-year cut lies outside the atlas's search space. The cycle 4 ruling on gold_autumn_physical_demand applies here: the atlas Bonferroni bar (design t >= 3.7) covers re-slices of that space, so it does not bind; the programme pass bar (design t >= 2) does. The participant is dated and obligated and trades in Tokyo hours, the only kind of flow that has survived in this store. The pre-registration also carries a same-window control, gotobi separation, month-window clustering and a cross replication. The closest priors are already measured. In patterns_usdjpy, the fix-short to 06:00 UTC made +0.056 R (t 2.5) in design and -0.004 R in check on all days, and +0.022 / -0.048 R on non-gotobi days. So the plain Tokyo-session short is a cost-level effect that faded after 2017. Only the fiscal excess over the control can carry this test.

Calendar and cost counts on USDJPY M15, design 2010-2017. I counted dates, spreads and ATR only; no returns were computed. Every hypothesis slot is tradeable: ye_short mar n10 80/80, mar_sep n10 160/160, ctrl n10 471/480; ny_long mar n10 80/80, ctrl n10 466/479 (the gaps are the January 2010 ATR warm-up). The gotobi share is balanced between hypothesis and control: ye_short n10 30.0% vs 31.0%, ny_long n10 22.5% vs 23.2%. Gotobi therefore cancels in the rule-2 difference, and rule 3 tests it separately. The median ATR20 at entry is 87 pips, so the 0.25 x ATR stop is about 22 pips, not the 17 pips the rationale assumes. The mean fill spread is 0.68 pips at 00:00 UTC and 0.63 pips at 06:00 UTC. The round trip is about 1.06 pips of spread and slippage plus about 0.75 pip of commission, about 1.8 pips. That is about 0.08 R at sl 0.25 and 0.04 R at sl 0.5. On the crosses at sl 0.25 it is about 0.07 R for EURJPY (ATR 142 pips, fill spread 1.2-1.3), 0.10 R for AUDJPY (ATR 111, 1.5-1.6) and 0.08 R for GBPJPY (ATR 174, 2.1-2.4). A net +0.10 R therefore needs about +0.18 R gross, about 4 pips per Tokyo session, and the 1.5x hard gate removes another 0.04 R.

The ny_long control is contaminated in two ways. (a) It keeps January and July, the calendar-year and half-year starts. New-period allocations are made then: January Toshin launches and, from 2014, NISA flows. That is the mechanism under test. The proposal itself drops June and December from the month-end control for the same reason, but it keeps their month-start counterparts. (b) Tokyo is closed on 20.0% (n5) and 13.3% (n10) of the original ny_long control dates in design, and on 21.7% and 15.3% in check. The closures are 1-3 January, Golden Week (3-5 May), 3 November, 11 February and Coming-of-Age Day. The April and April+October cells have 0-5%. A control diluted with no-flow days pulls the control toward zero and biases the rule-2 difference toward the hypothesis. Months {2, 6, 8, 11, 12} have a 3.5-3.8% holiday share in design (3.3-5.0% in check), with 200 (n5) and 400 (n10) design slots. The ye_short control {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11} is fine as it stands. Its holiday share (0.4-2.5%) is lower than in the March cells (8.8%, the Vernal Equinox) and the March+September cells (11.9%), so any bias works against the hypothesis.

Raw-sign gates in check and the holdout would test USDJPY drift as much as the fiscal flow. In trending years the Tokyo-session share of USDJPY's drift is about 1.5-2 pips per session (2013 was +22% on the year, 2022 +14%). At the 0.25 stop that is 0.05-0.08 R, the same size as the hypothesised effect. ny_long is long USDJPY through the 2021-2023 rally in check, and ye_short is short against it. A raw 'check avg R > 0' gate therefore favours ny_long whether or not an April flow exists. The control difference cancels drift. It should decide in check and in the holdout as well as in design, as the cycle 4 review required for the gold seasonal (window minus rest in check and holdout).

The kill rules and the pipeline do not line up, in three places. (a) Rule 1 picks one best cell across both legs, but rule 7 says the legs are separate claims, so the losing leg is never judged on its own. (b) Rule 1 requires 80 trades, which excludes the mar n5 cells (40 trades). The pipeline's stage B/C selection admits them (min_design_n is 30). The cell the pipeline validates on USDJPY can therefore differ from the rule-1 cell. Under month-window clustering, mar n5 and mar n10 share the same 8 clusters, so the 80-trade floor protects nothing the clustered t does not already protect. (c) With both legs in the B/C spec grid, stage B can pick different legs on different markets, and the walk-forward (4-year train, 1-year test, re-optimised by t) can switch legs from year to year. The pooled check and walk-forward hard gates would then test a mix of two claims with opposite signs on different dates.

Rule 4b (drop the best two month-windows) is too blunt for the 8-window March cells. Suppose the effect is real at +0.10 R and month-window means have an sd of about 0.22 R (0.7 R / sqrt(10)). The expected top two of 8 such windows sit about +1.4 and +0.85 sd above the mean. Dropping them leaves an expected mean of about +0.02 R, so the rule kills a true effect about half the time. Dropping only the single best window already catches the one-episode case, such as a March 2011 or March 2020 outlier. For the 16-window March+September cells, dropping two is reasonable.

Power and value are low. There are 8 independent Marches in design (16 with September). At the registered +0.10 R and t 1.2-1.5, the chance of reaching the pass bar (design t >= 2) is about 25% even if the effect is real, and rules 1-6 together will kill a real effect more often than not. If it does pass, 10-20 trades a year at about +0.1 R adds +1-2 R a year. Also, 30% of ye_short dates are gotobi days, when the basket's gotobi leg is already short USDJPY, so that part stacks risk rather than diversifying it. The rationale's claim that month-end Tokyo flows are larger than ordinary gotobi flows is not supported: +0.176 R (t 1.72, 94 trades) against +0.144 R for all gotobi days is a gap well inside noise. Approval rests on cheap compute and on closing the last unscanned calendar dimension, as the Director's note intends, not on an expected tradeable edge.
reviews.revisions: 1) Control months by leg. 'ctrl' means H_short = {1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11} for ye_short (unchanged) and H_long = {2, 6, 8, 11, 12} for ny_long. This drops the January and July new-period starts and the Golden Week month, and adds the ordinary non-quarter month-starts of June and December. The grid stays at 24 cells. Expected ny_long ctrl slots: design about 200 (n5) and 400 (n10); check 150 and 300. 2) Kill rules apply per leg. Rule 1 for each leg: the eligible cells are that leg's 8 hypothesis cells (months in {mar, mar_sep}). Set the minimum to 40 design trades (min_trades_design_per_market = 40). The chosen cell is the one with the highest trade-level design t, the same ranking the pipeline uses. It must have design avg R > 0, trade-level t >= 1 and month-window-clustered t >= 1. Rules 2-6 then use that leg's chosen cell and its matching ctrl cell (same leg, n_days and sl_atr). 3) Control difference in check and holdout. Add to rule 2: kill if check avg R(chosen) - check avg R(matching ctrl cell) <= 0. The stage A backtests span design and check, so read all 24 stage A rows from the trials table (stage 'A'); the report keeps only the top 15. If the leg is promoted, the locked run also runs the matching ctrl cell on the holdout years (same touch, counted). A holdout where chosen minus ctrl <= 0 is a fail even if the raw holdout avg R > 0. 4) Rule 4b: drop the best ceil(W/8) design month-windows, where W is the number of month-windows in the cell (1 for mar cells, 2 for mar_sep cells). Design avg R must stay > 0. Rule 4a (at least half the design years positive) stays. 5) Spec grids. stage_a = {market: USDJPY, grid: the full 24 cells}. The spec grid for stages B and C, the walk-forward and any holdout holds one leg only: {leg: [ye_short], months: [mar, mar_sep], n_days: [5, 10], sl_atr: [0.25, 0.5]} (8 cells). ye_short is the primary claim because its participants face a balance-sheet deadline. If ye_short fails rules 1-5 at stage A but the automatic floor lets the pipeline continue (an ny_long or ctrl cell cleared t >= 1), ignore its B/C output and scrap ye_short under rule 1. If ny_long passes rules 1-5 at stage A, it gets its own counted B/C run with leg [ny_long] in the same 8-cell shape. Read rule 6 at the leg's rule-1 cell on each cross from the stage B trials table. Pool the three crosses date-clustered: average the same-date R across crosses, then compute t over dates. 6) Expectations. Replace the cost line with: USDJPY stop about 22 pips at sl 0.25 (median design ATR20 87 pips); round trip about 1.8 pips, about 0.08 R at sl 0.25 and 0.04 R at sl 0.5; crosses 0.07-0.10 R at sl 0.25; +0.10 R net needs about +0.18 R gross, about 4 pips per Tokyo session. Add: P(design t >= 2 | effect real at +0.10 R) is about 25%; a positive below the bar is recorded as below the bar and not promoted. Delete the claim that the month-end-only gotobi variant shows larger month-end flows. 7) Exit guard. Also skip the date if m.ts[xi] is more than 60 minutes after d 06:00 UTC, so a data gap cannot stretch the hold into the next session. My count found no such date in design, so this changes nothing in practice. 8) Diagnostics, reported and not gating: for each leg's chosen cell, avg R and count on (a) Japanese public holidays inside the window (Vernal Equinox in late March, the September holidays, Sports Day; 8.8% of ye_short mar n10 dates and 11.9% of mar_sep n10 dates) and (b) Good Friday and Easter Monday dates (3 of 80 ye_short mar n10 dates, 8 of 80 ny_long mar n10 dates); plus a per-year table of chosen minus ctrl in design and check.
reviews.notes_for_builder: Contract details. (1) dates = np.unique(F.utc_dates(m)), keep F.weekday(dates) < 5 and dates >= np.datetime64(p['start']). month = (dates.astype('datetime64[M]').astype(np.int64) % 12) + 1. k = F.kth_last_weekday(dates) and rank = np.busday_count(dates.astype('datetime64[M]').astype('datetime64[D]'), dates). Both are calendar-based, so a missing data day does not shift them. ye_short selects 0 <= k < n_days; ny_long selects rank < n_days. (2) Month sets come from a per-leg mapping: {'mar': ({3}, {4}), 'mar_sep': ({3, 9}, {4, 10}), 'ctrl': ({1, 2, 5, 7, 8, 11}, {2, 6, 8, 11, 12})}. The first set is for ye_short, the second for ny_long. Raise on an unknown leg or months value. (3) eh, em = F.parse_hhmm(p['entry_utc']) and xh, xm = F.parse_hhmm(p['exit_utc']). ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, sel_dates, eh, em) and xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, sel_dates, xh, xm). Skip the date if ei < 1, ei >= m.n, xi >= m.n, xi <= ei, m.ts[ei] - (d + entry time) > p['max_delay_min'] minutes, or m.ts[xi] - (d + exit time) > 60 minutes. sig = ei - 1. Set entry_short[sig] (ye_short) or entry_long[sig] (ny_long), entry_type 0, valid_bars 1, tp_dist NaN, max_bars 0. The exit flag goes on xi - 1 (exit_short or exit_long), which is >= ei because xi > ei. (4) daily = F.daily_bars(m); atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, p['atr_n'])). Skip if atr[ei] is not finite or <= 0. sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * atr[ei]. Read atr at ei, not sig: ei's trading day starts at 17:00 NY the previous evening, so the value is known before entry. (5) PARAMS must contain every key: leg, months, n_days, sl_atr, entry_utc, exit_utc, max_delay_min, atr_n, start. Read every key from p; no holiday table and no randomness. A Python loop over selected dates is fine. The n5 cells are half of these. A count far from these numbers means the date selection is wrong.
